What is AI?: Artificial Intelligence is the simulation of human intelligence in machines, enabling them to perform tasks that typically require human intelligence.
What is machine learning?: Machine learning is a branch of AI where systems learn patterns from data to make predictions or decisions without explicit programming.
Who created Python?: Python was created by Guido van Rossum and first released in 1991.
What is Data Science?: Data Science is an interdisciplinary field that uses scientific methods, algorithms, and systems to extract knowledge and insights from structured and unstructured data.
What is NLP?: Natural Language Processing (NLP) is a field of AI that focuses on the interaction between computers and human (natural) languages.
What is supervised learning?: Supervised learning trains models on labeled data where the desired outputs are known.
What is unsupervised learning?: Unsupervised learning finds patterns or groupings in unlabeled data, such as clustering or dimensionality reduction.
What is reinforcement learning?: Reinforcement learning trains agents to make sequences of decisions by rewarding desired behaviors.
What is overfitting?: Overfitting happens when a model learns noise in the training data and performs poorly on new data.
What is cross-validation?: Cross-validation is a technique to evaluate model performance by splitting data into training and validation sets multiple times.
What is a neural network?: A neural network is a set of algorithms modeled after the human brain that is designed to recognize patterns.
What is deep learning?: Deep learning is a subset of machine learning using multi-layered neural networks to learn hierarchical representations.
What is a confusion matrix?: A confusion matrix is a table used to evaluate classification models by showing true vs predicted labels.
What is precision and recall?: Precision measures correctness of positive predictions; recall measures how many actual positives were identified.
What is feature engineering?: Feature engineering is the process of using domain knowledge to create features that make machine learning algorithms work better.
Why use Python for AI?: Python has rich libraries, simple syntax, and a strong community, making it ideal for AI and data science development.
What is TF-IDF?: TF-IDF (Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency) is a numerical statistic that reflects how important a word is to a document in a collection.
What is cosine similarity?: Cosine similarity measures similarity between two vectors by computing the cosine of the angle between them—common in text matching.
How to handle missing data?: Common strategies include removal, imputation (mean/median/mode), or model-based methods depending on context.
What is tokenization?: Tokenization is splitting text into smaller units (tokens), such as words or sentences, as a first preprocessing step in NLP.
What is classification?: Classification is a supervised learning task where the goal is to predict which category or class an input belongs to based on labeled training data.
What is regression?: Regression is a supervised learning task used to predict continuous numerical values, such as price, temperature, or sales forecasts.
What is clustering?: Clustering is an unsupervised learning technique that groups similar data points together without predefined labels.
What is a decision tree?: A decision tree is a model that makes predictions by recursively splitting data based on feature values, creating a tree-like structure.
What is a random forest?: A random forest is an ensemble learning method that combines multiple decision trees to improve accuracy and reduce overfitting.
What is ensemble learning?: Ensemble learning combines predictions from multiple models to achieve better accuracy than a single model alone.
What is the bias-variance tradeoff?: The bias-variance tradeoff is the balance between a model's ability to fit training data and its ability to generalize to new data.
What is gradient descent?: Gradient descent is an optimization algorithm that iteratively adjusts model parameters to minimize loss by moving in the direction of steepest descent.
What are hyperparameters?: Hyperparameters are configuration settings chosen before training a model, such as learning rate, number of layers, or regularization strength.
What is dimensionality reduction?: Dimensionality reduction techniques reduce the number of features in a dataset while retaining important information, improving efficiency and performance.
What is the difference between training: The training set is used to teach the model, while the test set evaluates how well the model performs on unseen data.
What is normalization and standardizatio: Normalization scales features to a range like [0,1], while standardization transforms features to have mean 0 and standard deviation 1.
